name: Brute Force: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries use repetitive password guessing against SSH or other authentication services to obtain valid credentials.
linux_indicators: Multiple sshd 'Failed password' or 'Invalid user' entries from one source IP
containment_steps: Block offending source IP via ufw/nftables
Enforce SSH key-only authentication and fail2ban

name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
description: Adversaries try one or a few common passwords across many usernames to evade per-account lockout thresholds.
linux_indicators: Failed sshd logins targeting 4+ distinct usernames from one IP
containment_steps: Rate-limit SSH connections
Audit targeted accounts for weak passwords or unexpected logins

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries use compromised legitimate credentials to log in and blend with normal administrative activity.
linux_indicators: Accepted password/publickey following brute-force attempts or from anomalous external IP
containment_steps: Terminate active sessions for compromised user
Rotate passwords/SSH keys and inspect recent commands

name: Remote Services: SSH
description: Adversaries use SSH to interactively access remote Linux hosts or pivot internally.
linux_indicators: Unexpected sshd Accepted sessions or outbound SSH connections
containment_steps: Restrict SSH access via AllowUsers/bastion firewall rules
Review ~/.ssh/known_hosts and active PTYs

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
description: Adversaries exploit misconfigured sudoers rules or cached credentials to execute commands as root.
containment_steps: Audit /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d
Remove unauthorized privileges and revoke sudo tokens

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
description: Adversaries execute bash/sh scripts, piped downloaders (curl|bash), base64 payloads, or reverse shells.
linux_indicators: auditd EXECVE or sudo commands invoking curl|bash, /dev/tcp, nc -e, or base64 -d
containment_steps: Kill malicious child processes
Capture volatile script artifacts and check outbound C2 connections

name: OS Credential Dumping: /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow
description: Adversaries read /etc/shadow or /etc/gshadow to extract password hashes for offline cracking.
linux_indicators: sudo or auditd EXECVE reading /etc/shadow or /etc/gshadow
containment_steps: Assume local password hashes are exposed; force password rotation for accounts with hashes

name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
description: Adversaries create or modify cron jobs to maintain persistence or run recurring malicious scripts.
containment_steps: Inspect all user crontabs and /etc/cron* directories
Remove unauthorized cron entries

name: Account Manipulation: SSH Authorized Keys
description: Adversaries add attacker-controlled public keys to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for stealthy persistent access.
linux_indicators: Commands or file writes referencing authorized_keys
containment_steps: Audit ~/.ssh/authorized_keys across all users including root
Remove unrecognized public keys

name: Create Account: Local Account
description: Adversaries create hidden or service-like local Linux accounts to maintain access after initial remediation.
linux_indicators: useradd events in auth.log or auditd
containment_steps: Lock and remove unauthorized accounts (usermod -L / userdel)
Review /etc/sudoers group memberships

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries download external tools, payloads, or scripts onto the compromised host via curl, wget, or scp.
linux_indicators: curl or wget fetching remote scripts or binaries from external IPs/domains
containment_steps: Block destination C2 IP/domain
Hash and quarantine downloaded artifacts in /tmp or /dev/shm

name: Indicator Removal: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs
description: Adversaries truncate, delete, or alter /var/log/auth.log, wtmp, or bash_history to hide intrusion tracks.
linux_indicators: truncate, shred, rm, or echo > targeting /var/log/* or ~/.bash_history
containment_steps: Preserve remote syslog/journald backups
Check filesystem metadata and auditd logs

name: Impair Defenses
description: Adversaries attempt to disable security controls, firewalls, auditd, or inject misleading instructions into AI/log triage pipelines.
linux_indicators: Prompt-injection strings in SSH usernames/commands or stopping auditd/ufw/fail2ban
containment_steps: Verify security services (auditd, ufw, SIEM forwarder) are active
Treat prompt-injection attempts as hostile activity

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries scan local or adjacent subnets for open ports and internal services after gaining shell access.
linux_indicators: Execution of nmap, masscan, or ss/netstat sweeps
containment_steps: Check lateral network flows from the host
Segment internal services

name: Account Discovery: Local Account
description: Adversaries enumerate local users, groups, and sudo privileges via id, whoami, /etc/passwd, or getent.
linux_indicators: Burst execution of id, groups, getent passwd, sudo -l
containment_steps: Correlate discovery commands with preceding authentication events

name: Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service
description: Adversaries install malicious systemd unit files to execute payloads automatically on boot.
linux_indicators: Writes to /etc/systemd/system/*.service or systemctl enable of unknown units
containment_steps: Audit /etc/systemd/system and systemctl list-unit-files
Disable and remove unauthorized unit files
